4bca48cc4007: Here the story leaves the harbour in Esbjerg and winds back to 1883. For while Thomas’ trail ran through tax books and registers, another part of the family of brothers and sisters had long since set off the opposite way — inland.
94428931a5fa: <t1>Ane Johanne</t1> was Niels Thomsen Silkjær’s eldest daughter with Ane Jensen. She stands in the middle of the line this chronicle follows — and she is the one the sources say least about.
df59896f45f1: Born at Økjær on 22 October 1883, baptised in Husby Church on 18 November — daughter of Niels and his second wife, Ane Jensen. We know her dates, her marriage, her children. We do not know her voice: no letters, no memories. But in one place in the sources her imprint can be glimpsed, and we will come back to it.
34562b92f4dc: On 22 March 1906 she was married in Husby Church, 22 years old. The groom did not come from the coast: <t1>Mads Erik Madsen</t1>, born on 28 July 1879 in Hanning parish and baptised in Hanning Church on 17 August, son of Knud Madsen and Ane Eriksen. He was a <t2>bricklayer</t2> — later a master mason at Rækker Mølle. At the census of 1901 he was living on Sofievej in Copenhagen: he had been out in the world before he came back and fetched a wife from Husby.
6db749a3153f: All the women before her in this story had married within the same landscape: from Tarpgaard to Økjær, from Økjær to Husby Klit. Ane Johanne married a <t1>trade</t1> — and a trade did not live in any particular place.
eacdb757ddec: A bricklayer followed the work, and in those years the building was happening inland: in the railway towns, along the new lines, in the growing country parishes on the reclaimed heath. She became the first in the direct line to leave the coast altogether.
c17a70092502: The road can be followed in the children’s parishes of birth — and in the censuses, which show Ane Johanne in Husby in 1890 and the family in Sædding in 1911, 1916, 1921 and 1925, and in Vorgod in 1930.
11a602b9fb1a: Dune, marsh and surf. Ane Johanne is born and marries.
c9b2a0679be4: Forty kilometres to the south-east, Sædding parish. Mill and dairy instead of a landing beach. Bricks instead of nets.
421993de1643: Another stretch inland, into the parishes of the heath reclamation. The census of 1930 finds the family here — and here both husband and wife died.
d34a3f64a334: The direction is clear: away from the sea, into the Denmark that was building. And now to the place where the sources come closest to Ane Johanne.
0012a88a4bd1: The children took the surname Madsen — that was the rule. But someone chose to set the mother’s family name in the middle of the boy’s name, for a child born forty kilometres from the farm, in a parish where the name meant nothing to anyone else.
8f818542899d: That choice of name is the closest we come to an imprint from her side of the family: someone wrote her family’s place into her son’s name — perhaps she herself, perhaps the parents together. She had left Økjær, and the place travelled with her.
e77bfd18f7cc: And then she had fourteen children.
f2d814a08e65: The eldest, Anne, came in 1907, the year after the wedding. The youngest, Elisabeth, in 1925. Eighteen years, fourteen births, three parishes — eleven of the children came into the world between 1907 and 1918.
091f4b5f8bca: The family scattered, as large families did: Niels Silkjær to Ikast, Dagmar and Laura stayed in the Vorgod district, Christian ended up in Videbæk — and Knud, the second eldest, died in 1973 in Calgary in Canada. The son of the mason from Rækker Mølle lies buried on the far side of the Atlantic.
634fddc61668: Mads Erik died on 2 August 1951. Ane Johanne outlived him by five years and died on 19 November 1956. The Ikast district, with which the family is later associated, did not come through her but through her son Niels Silkjær Madsen: he married in Isenvad Church in 1933 and died in Ikast in 1972.
7a17e258f404: Read more about the traces in the parish registers<t1/>
e12594e5ef57: The son Niels Silkjær Madsen was born on 2 April 1909 in Sædding parish, Bølling Hundred — according to the parish register index. The daughter Laura is confirmed in the original baptismal entry in the Sædding parish register: born on 25 March 1917 at Rækker Mølle as the daughter of Mads Erik Madsen and Ane Johanne. The traces towards the Ikast district still rest on indexes, not on original entries.

0e7c20019dea: Among the fourteen children of the master mason Mads Erik and Ane Johanne was a daughter, <t1>Laura</t1> — the tenth in the row. She was born on 25 March 1917 at Rækker Mølle in Sædding parish; the baptismal entry names her parents as Mads Erik Madsen and Ane Johanne. [S161]
8d5d935f7cee: She was a domestic help. On 29 December 1938 she was married in <t1>Vorgod Church</t1> to <t2>Laurids Mikkelsen</t2>, born on 11 September 1911 at Fjelstervang in the same parish, owner of the farm Nygaard. She had followed her parents inland and found her husband where they had come to rest.
01dffcc63c22: They had five children: Knud, born on 19 November 1943 in Sædding, Birte in 1945, Ernst in 1947, Edith in 1949 and Leif in 1956. Notice who was given the name. Only the eldest and the youngest have <t1>Silkjær</t1> in their own names — Knud Silkjær Mikkelsen and Leif Silkjær Mikkelsen. The three in the middle were not given it. The name did not pass on evenly; it was set on two of five, thirteen years apart.

7d8ad88f7650: Laura did not herself carry Silkjær in her official name; it was her mother’s, not hers. Nothing required her to carry it on. Two of her five children had it written into their own all the same.
ef6962f98442: Laurids died on 22 September 1996. Laura followed the year after, on 30 September 1997, in Vorgod — ninety-one years after her mother left the coast, and forty kilometres from the marsh the name came from. They lie together in the churchyard at Fjelstervang under four lines and three words.
